claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation in the eutectic high-entropy alloy arises from thermally induced weakening of inter-phase boundaries.
Elevated temperature promotes differential thermal expansion between the phases.
Elevated temperature promotes selective oxidation at inter-phase boundaries.
Selective boundary oxidation produces brittle, adherent oxide patches.
Mechanical loading cracks the oxide patches formed at inter-phase boundaries.
Cracking of the oxide exposes fresh metal.
Freshly exposed substrate corrodes rapidly in the aggressive environment.
Damaged inter-phase boundaries concentrate local stresses.
Boundary damage and stress concentration increase abrasive wear.
Repeated oxide cracking, fresh-metal exposure, corrosion, and wear form a self-reinforcing degradation cycle.
The initial alloy has an interdigitated multiphase eutectic microstructure with well-defined inter-phase boundaries.
Homogenization heat treatment or modified alloying can reduce the density or severity of inter-phase boundaries.
A temperature around 500°C is high enough to promote significant oxidation kinetics and thermal-expansion mismatch in the proposed system.
The proposed effect requires a corrosive environment containing a sufficient concentration of chloride ions or another aggressive species.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic sample with prominent phase boundaries will exhibit greater total degradation.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic sample will exhibit a higher wear rate and greater material removal.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic sample will exhibit a higher corrosion rate, reflected by greater corrosion current density or mass loss.
Preferential localized corrosion will occur at cracked oxide sites associated with inter-phase boundaries.
The precise changes in wear loss and corrosion current depend on alloy composition and test environment.
Failure to observe lower wear and corrosion in the homogenized sample, or failure to observe preferential boundary-oxide cracking, would refute the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The proposed control is described as compositionally matched or similar, but modified alloying is offered as an alternative way to reduce boundary density. Modified alloying changes composition and introduces a compositional confound, so that option is not a strictly matched microstructure-only comparison.
